chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rabi' and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The time for the Dhuhr prayer on the day of Friday is when the sun declines.
ai.seo_question: When does the time for Friday Dhuhr prayer begin according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the time for the Friday Dhuhr prayer commences precisely at solar zenith (Zawal), aligning with the general rule for Dhuhr but emphasizing its distinct timing for the congregational Friday prayer. Scholars note this establishes the canonical start of the Friday prayer window, distinguishing it from the regular Dhuhr time which may begin slightly earlier in some schools, thereby ensuring the Imam leads the prayer at the optimal moment of the day's peak. This ruling underscores the importance of communal unity in Shia jurisprudence, as the Friday prayer is a mandatory congregational act with specific temporal parameters.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, altogether, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said:
‘The time for Al-Zohr on the day of Friday is when the sun (starts to) decline’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘i and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah all who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The time of al-Dhuhr on Friday begins at Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime).”
